chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn ruled regarding a man who entered the house of some people without their permission and their dog injured him, and he said: “There is no liability upon them; but if he entered with their permission, they are liable.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in the context of legal judgment
key_terms.فَعَقَرَهُ: then it injured or mauled him
key_terms.لَا ضَمَانَ: there is no legal liability or compensation due

ai.seo_question: Is a homeowner liable if their dog injures someone who entered the house without permission?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn concerning liability for injury caused by a household dog. It establishes that the owners are not liable when someone enters without permission, but they are liable if the person entered with their permission.
